current_operational_flow.description: Two parallel mission execution paths existed; now unified under MissionController as official path

path_a_official.name: MissionController (mission_controller.py) - OFFICIAL PATH
components: MissionTaskAgent pool (12 agents with deterministic failure injection)
Failure taxonomy: TASK_EXECUTION_FAILURE, TOOL_RUNTIME_FAILURE, PLAN_DEVIATION, PROCESS_INTERRUPTION
Recovery actions: RETRY, REASSIGN, REPLAN, RESUME
Full checkpoint with task definitions, dependencies, attempt history, human_gate, human_decision
path_a_official.state_machine: RECEIVED → ANALYZING → PLANNING → DESIGNING → REVIEWING → APPROVED → AWAITING_APPROVAL → EXECUTING → EXECUTED → VERIFYING → EVIDENCED (stops, VERIFIED is owner-gated, actor='user')
path_a_official.human_gate: Full - create_human_gate()/decide_human_gate() via ExecutionEngine, durable via checkpoint
path_a_official.drives_to: EVIDENCED (owner-gated VERIFIED reserved for human actor)

path_b_legacy.name: OperationalMissionPlanner Path (operational.py) - LEGACY / BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY ONLY
components: OperationalImplementerAgent (writes files, runs commands via sandbox)
path_b_legacy.state_machine: RECEIVED → ANALYZING → PLANNING → DESIGNING → REVIEWING → APPROVED → AWAITING_APPROVAL → EXECUTING → EXECUTED → VERIFYING → EVIDENCED (stops, VERIFIED requires actor='user')
path_b_legacy.drives_to: EVIDENCED (fixed: was incorrectly driving to VERIFIED with actor='system')
path_b_legacy.checkpoint_resume: Uses ExecutionEngine checkpoints (partial - no MissionController replan/resume capabilities)
limitations: No failure classification or replan capability
Cannot handle mission deviation - only simple linear missions

shared_foundation.ExecutionEngine: Core orchestration (mission/run/task lifecycle, agent execution, tool invocation, artifacts, evidence, verification, state machine, events, checkpoint/resume)
shared_foundation.state_machine: MissionState and TaskState enums with validated transitions (golden rule: VERIFIED only by actor='user')
shared_foundation.event_catalog: FactoryEvent with full event types including HumanGateCreatedEvent, HumanDecisionRecordedEvent

integration_decision.decision: MissionController is the single official mission execution path. OperationalExecutionEngine delegates to it by default (use_mission_controller=True). Legacy path retained only for backward compatibility with explicit opt-in.
rationale: MissionController provides the complete E33-verified autonomy stack (failure detection, classification, replan, checkpoint, resume, no-false-re-execution, completion verification)
OperationalExecutionEngine duplicates mission lifecycle logic but lacks the autonomy capabilities proven in E33
MissionController's declarative TaskSpec is more expressive and testable than OperationalMissionPlanner templates
MissionController drives to EVIDENCED (correct owner-gated VERIFIED semantics) while OperationalExecutionEngine previously drove to VERIFIED autonomously (incorrect, now fixed)
Single source of truth for mission execution eliminates competing authorities
Future UI/API consumers need one official path, not two
Golden rule (VERIFIED only by actor='user') enforced in state machine - neither path can autonomously grant VERIFIED
integration_decision.architecture: MissionController is the authoritative mission execution service. OperationalExecutionEngine wraps it for backward compatibility and simple use cases. All new development uses MissionController path.

verification_authority.VERIFIED_transition: ONLY allowed when actor='user' (golden rule enforced in validate_mission_transition in domain_model.py:795-797)
verification_authority.EVIDENCED_transition: Allowed by system/agent after verification completes
verification_authority.owner_gated: MissionController.finalize_mission() stops at EVIDENCED; human (actor='user') must transition to VERIFIED
verification_authority.legacy_path: Fixed to stop at EVIDENCED; cannot bypass golden rule
